records.text: In late fall 2024, Victor Marx told Corby Hall that he needed 50 rifles for a Haiti mission where the firearms would be dropped off and left.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: Pretty early on, you know, he was there for probably four or four-ish hours and, you know, when we got, when we got alone on the shop floor and between the machines, he's like, hey, you know, I still, I still got this 80 stuff going on and I need 50 guns to take and drop off in Haiti. ... And I said, well, you know, that, that's a embargo country.

In the late fall of 2024, Mr. Marx (Victor Marx) flew into the airport in Henderson, Texas, to tour the FoldAR facilities. ... During this time, Mr. Marx (Victor Marx) stated to me that he needed 50 rifles for a mission to Haiti where he would drop off and leave the firearms. ... I responded that it would constitute illegal exporting to do that, so I couldn't help him, and I advised him to not do it with any other firearms as well.

verification.notes: Hall publicly repeated that Marx requested 50 guns to take and drop off in Haiti and that Hall refused because of export restrictions. Marx later acknowledged wanting to bring weapons to Haiti but denied trafficking and disputed the framing. The request for Haiti weapons is corroborated at the allegation level; the exact drop-off-and-leave terms remain contested.

sources.relevance: Records Hall allegation and Marx response acknowledging he wanted to bring weapons to Haiti while denying trafficking.

records.text: Victor Marx told Corby Hall that a long-range rifle and camera would be used to kill anyone scaling a Haitian orphanage fence and that the video would serve as deterrent propaganda.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: He wants to blow the head off of somebody that sticks their head up over the fence around this orphanage in Haiti. ... shooting somebody climbing over got it on camera we can distribute it out in the 80 land and they won't jump over anymore like like i see the good intention behind it but yeah no

He stated to me that long-range rifle and camera would be used to blow the head off of someone if they attempted to scale the fence of the orphanage. Then the video would be used as propaganda to deter further attempts by gangs around the area.

verification.notes: Hall repeated this account publicly and provided a detailed description of the proposed rifle, scope camera, and alleged statement. Marx denied illegal arms activity, and no recording, message, independent witness, or operational record was found that conclusively establishes the private conversation. Unable to verify beyond Hall allegation.

records.text: Victor Marx told Corby Hall that Marx's team was going to capture or execute Jimmy Chérizier.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: He then explained that his team was actually going to capture or execute Jimmy Barbecue, the top gang leader of Haiti.

verification.notes: Hall later repeated that Marx discussed shooting or capturing Jimmy Cherizier. Public reporting confirms Marx subsequently traveled to Haiti and met Cherizier, but no recording, message, or independent witness confirms what Marx privately told Hall before the trip. Unable to verify the private statement.

records.text: Victor Marx said he traveled to Haiti after an orphanage urgently requested help in response to an imminent threat from the 400 Mawozo gang.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: The reason I'm here in Haiti doing all this high-risk missionary stuff is a while back we responded to the urgent requests of an orphanage that was under imminent threat. ... Of attack by what many consider the most notorious gang in Haiti, the 400 Mawozo. It broke my heart to think of the possibilities were this gang to attack to take control over that area.

verification.notes: The statement is attributional and is supported by public mission coverage: Marx traveled to Haiti, presented the mission as protecting orphanages and vulnerable people amid gang threats, and met leaders associated with Cherizier and 400 Mawozo. The source confirms his public explanation, not every detail of the claimed urgent request.

sources.title: CBN News: Victor Marx Haiti mission
sources.relevance: Confirms the trip, its publicly stated orphanage-protection purpose, and meetings involving Cherizier and 400 Mawozo.

records.text: Victor Marx denied ever seeking to traffic rifles or other arms to Haiti, Israel, or Iran.
records.speaker: Victor Marx

appearances.snippet: Of course not. It's illegal. How would I even be where I am today for years of working with federal, state, local authorities?

verification.notes: The primary episode contains a recorded interview in which Victor Marx is asked whether he ever sought to traffic rifles or arms to Haiti, Israel, or Iran and answers of course not. This verifies that he issued the denial; it does not adjudicate the underlying arms allegations.
